the expression of stress- and apoptosis related genes were affected by air exposure, but there was no significant change in cortisol levels.
the embryos of Atlantic Cod, Gadus morhau L., have a potential to express stress- and apoptosis related genes in response to air exposure.

(a) the embryos of Atlantic salmon, Gadus morhu a L., respond to a short-term air exposure by increasing expression of stress and apoptotic genes, and (b) the embryos of cod do not show a significant increase in total cortisol level following air exposure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the early life stage of cod, a commercially important species, which has been used as a model to study the stress response in teleost fishes.
the identification of potential molecular biomarkers that could be used for assessing the stress status of fish embryos.
the development of biomarkers of stress and the effects of stress in early life stages of fish.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
air exposure at 2 min does not affect the expression of genes related to the stress response and apoptosis in Atlantic cod embryos.
the embryos of Atlantic salmon are capable of responding to stress at a very early stage of development, even before hatching, as indicated by the increased expression levels of the selected genes.
the embryos of Atlantic Cod are capable of responding to air exposure at an early developmental stage by up-regulating stress- and apoptosis related genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
air exposure is not a significant stressor for cod embryos, but that the embryos have the potential for a significant stress response.
there is a significant increase in expression levels of genes related to stress, apoptosis and antioxidant defense in cod embryos following air exposure.

air exposure of cod embryos at a time when the embryos have not yet developed the ability to regulate their cortisol levels, results in a rapid increase in the expression of genes that are related to the stress response and apoptosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the embryos have the ability to respond to stress by up-regulation of stress-related genes, even though the stress response is not fully developed.
embryos of Atlantic cod have the potential to respond to environmental stressors, such as air exposure, and this response can be monitored using gene expression analysis.
there is a need to further investigate the expression of these genes in embryos of different developmental stages and in response to different stressors.
